Owner
cumin
cumin
«Agent»
Planner
«Agent»
Planner
«Agent»
Implementer
«Agent»
Implementer
«Agent»
Reviewer
«Agent»
Reviewer
Issue tracker
(GitHub Issues)
Issue tracker
(GitHub Issues)
Repository
(GitHub)
Repository
(GitHub)
A resident program on the Host (Mac mini).
launchd restarts it when it stops.
Later: send a heartbeat, watched from another machine.
May change to Jira or another tracker later.
The source code stays on GitHub.
1. Receive a requirement
write the requirement as an issue, add cumin/type/requirement
when done, add cumin/status/ready to the requirement issue
The only entry to cumin is an issue. No layout of the repository is assumed.
Adding cumin/status/ready means "submitted" (a draft is not picked up).
The Owner may keep requirement documents (for example requirements/) in the repository.
Linked from the issue, they are context that the agents read.
poll for issues with cumin/type/requirement and cumin/status/ready
cumin is resident and fetches work by itself.
The Owner does not start it.
2. Plan
change the label of the requirement issue from cumin/status/ready to cumin/status/planning
request: split this requirement
read the repository (with the documents that the requirement issue links)
create implementation issues as sub-issues (1 issue = 1 implementation task)
record the dependencies between the issues
add a provisional risk to each issue
Risk criteria:
risk/low = a few lines whose effect is obvious.
risk/high = a change that a revert cannot undo (database migration, deployment or CI setting,
authentication or payment, side effect on an external service, public API contract, rules of cumin).
risk/medium = everything else.
Split by policies/issue-sizing.md
(a risk/high change is isolated in its own smallest issue).
plan done (the agent run ended)
check that sub-issues exist and each has a risk
3. Check the plan
change the label of the requirement issue to cumin/status/awaiting-owner-review
notify: the split needs a check
check the split and the risks (the Owner fixes them if needed)
if good, add cumin/status/ready to the implementation issues
cumin/status/ready means three things:
the split is approved, the risk is final, and the implementation may start.
The Owner always takes part in the risk (a start).
It may go on only some sub-issues. When they are all closed and only
sub-issues without the label remain, cumin asks for a check again.
4. Implement and review
loop
[while an issue has cumin/status/ready, its dependencies are done, and AI resources are free]
AI resources are free = the usage of both quota windows of Claude Code is below its limit.
Weekly window: the pace limit = target x min(1, (elapsed + lead) / 7 days), so the week is used evenly.
5h window: the threshold of the current time band (higher when the Owner does not work).
The target, the lead, the thresholds, and the time bands are in the settings file of cumin.
cumin can read the usage (the result of a Claude Code run holds the usage and the reset time; measured).
choose the next issue that can start
change the label from cumin/status/ready to cumin/status/implementing
Changing the label is the claim. It comes before the request, so the same issue is never requested twice.
The status label is on the implementation issue, always exactly one. cumin changes all of them (never an agent).
An issue that already has a pull request continues from there (after the Owner sends it back or answers).
The agent then gets a new session and reads the issue, the pull request, and the comments again.
request: implement this issue
push a branch and open a pull request
implementation done (the agent run ended)
check that the pull request is open
change the label to cumin/status/awaiting-checks
wait until every required check passes (on a failure, ask the Implementer for a fix; with no required check, it passes at once)
An open pull request alone does not mean the implementation is done.
cumin decides from facts on GitHub, not from what an agent reports.
While the checks run, no agent runs, so no quota is used.
loop
[until no blocking comment is left (up to 3 rounds; the number will be tuned)]
change the label to cumin/status/reviewing
request: review this pull request
post the review (APPROVE when nothing blocks, REQUEST_CHANGES when a fix is needed)
review done (the agent run ended)
read the review of the current head commit
opt
[a comment to fix]
change the label to cumin/status/implementing
request: fix the comments
push the fix
fix done
change the label to cumin/status/awaiting-checks
wait until every required check passes
alt
[approved, risk/low]
merge (I6)
close the implementation issue once, when GitHub did not
[approved, risk/medium or risk/high]
change the label to cumin/status/awaiting-owner-review
notify: the merge needs a decision
approve the head commit with a review
merge at the next poll (I12)
close the implementation issue once, when GitHub did not
To send it back, comment on the pull request and add cumin/status/ready to the implementation issue again.
Whether risk/medium can move to an automatic merge is decided while running.
[blocking comments left after 3 rounds]
request: sort out what is not decided
post a short report for the Owner
change the label to cumin/status/awaiting-owner-decision
notify: a decision is needed
answer
add cumin/status/ready to the implementation issue again
after the merge, copy the remaining work (Follow-up and suggestions not taken) to the requirement issue as a follow-up note
While waiting for the Owner, cumin goes on with other issues that do not depend on it.
The Owner's "go ahead" is always adding cumin/status/ready.
5. Acceptance
Start: every sub-issue of the requirement issue is closed.
request: check the acceptance
check each item of Requirements of the requirement issue on the latest main
comment the result, the evidence, and the remaining work on the requirement issue
check done (the agent run ended)
check that the comment exists, change the label of the requirement issue to cumin/status/awaiting-owner-review
notify: the requirement can be accepted
alt
[accept]
close the requirement issue (= accepted)
Work from the follow-up notes that the Owner wants goes into a new requirement issue.
[send back]
add to the requirement issue, or add sub-issues
add cumin/status/ready to the added sub-issues
A send-back does not go through the Planner (a start).
Back to "4. Implement and review"; when every sub-issue is closed,
the acceptance notification comes again.
Exception: an agent cannot go on
change the label to cumin/status/awaiting-owner-decision
notify: blocked, a decision is needed
answer
add cumin/status/ready to the implementation issue again
Exception: the quota reached its limit
notify: the quota reached its limit, so no new issue starts
opt
[the Owner allows using up the current 5h window]
allow: use up the current 5h window
The allowance lasts until that 5h window resets. The 5h threshold becomes 100%.
Nothing raises the pace limit of the weekly window.
First, the Owner gives the allowance with a command on the Host (from outside through Tailscale and SSH).
Later: a Discord bot, so that the allowance comes from Discord.
When the window resets, or when the limit rises above the usage, cumin starts issues again by itself.
Exception: no issue can go on
notify: waiting
First, cumin only notifies and does nothing else.
Later: draft the next requirement issue from the requirement documents, and more.
A notification only says "come and look". The conversation is in issues and pull requests.
Notifications use a Discord webhook (replaceable later).
The identities on GitHub are apart from the Owner, one GitHub App for each role (policy):
cumin-core, cumin-planner, cumin-implementer, cumin-reviewer.
The target repository (peppercheck) is public, so rulesets work on the Free plan.
A ruleset limits updates of main to the Owner and cumin-core.
